title: Inference Cost & Latency Lab — Facilitation Notes
content:
Purpose:
Run a focused, outcome-driven 2.5 hour lab with a customer engineering + product team to align on cost vs latency tradeoffs for a target inference workload. Deliverables: clear routing/quantization recommendations, an experimental runbook, and a prioritized decision matrix for production rollout.

Audience:
Customer engineers, product PM, infra/cloud lead, solutions/Redwood SEs (2), optional data scientist. Max 10 attendees.

Pre-work (sent 5 days prior):
- Customer provides a short workload spec (QPS, typical prompt length distribution, p95 latency target, cost target).
- Customer shares 3 example prompts/responses and a sample traffic profile (CSV).
- Runbook template and small data-collection script (we provide) to collect token counts and sequence-length histogram.

Room setup & materials:
- Conference room with projector + whiteboard, or Zoom + Miro board for remote.
- Slide deck: 12 slides (see outline below).
- Miro board: "Decision Canvas" (sections: constraints, current ops, experiments, risks, next steps).
- Notebook for each small group, sticky notes.

High-level agenda (2.5 hours)
- 0:00–0:10 (10m): Kickoff & goals — introductions, success criteria, artifacts we will deliver.
- 0:10–0:35 (25m): Current state & assumptions — customer presents workload, infra, pain points (10m), SEs ask clarifying questions (15m).
- 0:35–1:05 (30m): Latency vs cost primer — interactive mini-talk: batching, quantization, model selection, routing tiers, caching patterns. Short demos of expected unit costs (Redwood numbers) and latency ranges.
- 1:05–1:20 (15m): Breakout #1 (small groups) — estimate cost/latency for 3 candidate configs (hosted small model, hosted medium model + quant, dedicated GPU pool). Output: 2-minute summary per group.
- 1:20–1:40 (20m): Group synth — collect estimates, reconcile large discrepancies, capture assumptions on Miro.
- 1:40–2:00 (20m): Experiment design — define 3 prioritized experiments (what to measure, acceptance criteria, duration, infra needed). Assign owners.
- 2:00–2:20 (20m): Rollout decision canvas — evaluate risk, rollback plan, SLA implications, monitoring needs.
- 2:20–2:30 (10m): Finalize next steps, immediate wins, and close.

Slide outline (for the deck we present)
- Slide 1: Title + outcomes we will produce (decision matrix PDF, experiment runbook, monitoring checklist).
- Slide 2: Agenda + timebox.
- Slide 3: Customer workload snapshot (QPS, token distribution, latency SLOs).
- Slide 4: Redwood inference primitives (batching, caching, quantization, routing) — visual callouts.
- Slide 5: Typical cost/latency envelope examples (two charts: cost per 1k tokens vs p95 latency).
- Slide 6: Tradeoff patterns & heuristics (when to choose dedicated vs hosted, quantization caveats).
- Slide 7: Experiment design template (metric, hypothesis, duration, dataset).
- Slide 8: Decision Canvas (columns: constraint, option, expected benefit, risk, owner).
- Slide 9: Monitoring & alerting checklist (token-level cost alerts, p95 drift, error spikes).
- Slide 10: Quick wins (config flags, cache TTLs, prompt edit guidelines).
- Slide 11: Next steps & owners.
- Slide 12: Appendix — runbook snippets, links to sample infra templates.

Facilitation notes & prompts (detailed)
- Kickoff: "Our goal is to leave with 3 experiments you can run in the next 2 weeks and a clear production decision path." Call out today's artifacts.
- Clarifying Qs for the customer-state slot: "What percentage of requests are cold-start vs warm? How tolerant is your UX to 200–400ms variance? Any regulatory constraints on model outputs or data residency?"
- During latency vs cost primer: show 1–2 real-world Redwood numbers (e.g., medium Llama variant: baseline cost X per 1k tokens, p95 Y ms on A100 vs 40% less cost when using int8 quant + 1.8x latency). Use these as discussion anchors (avoid promising exact numbers for customer's infra).
- Breakout #1 facilitation: groups must write a single-line assumption for each estimate. Prompt: "If your estimate assumes perfect caching, mark that as high risk."
- Group synth: Seek convergence. Use the whiteboard to map optimistic / pessimistic bounds. If teams disagree >2x on cost, add a quick diagnostic question to the Miro board to capture why.
- Experiment design cues: ensure each experiment has a success metric and a rollback criterion. Suggested experiments: enable prefix caching for 48h; quantize to 8-bit for a 24-hour A/B; configure a small dedicated pool with 95th-percentile capacity sizing test.
- Rollout canvas: have teams indicate "must-have" vs "nice-to-have" for latency and cost. If regulatory concerns exist, escalate to private-deployments track.

Outputs to produce at end of session (deliverables)
- 1-page Decision Matrix (PDF) listing recommended config and rationale.
- 3 Experiment runbooks (short templates: steps, metrics, expected delta, owner).
- Monitoring checklist and suggested Redwood Console dashboards to add.
- Short backlog of follow-ups: sample infra PR, security review, billing impact estimate.

Templates to attach to deliverables (we will fill in during session)
- Experiment runbook header (Name, Owner, Hypothesis, Metric, Baseline, Success Threshold, Duration, Infra notes).
- Decision matrix grid (Option, Expected Cost delta, Expected Latency delta, Risk, Implementation effort, Owner).
- Quick monitoring alerts (p95 latency > SLO for 10m, cost burn > budget rate for 1h).

Common pitfalls & how to avoid them (cheat sheet for SEs)
- Pitfall: Over-optimistic caching assumptions. Avoid by requiring a test that simulates production TTLs.
- Pitfall: Treating quantization as zero-effort. Log perf and quality hit, add sample evaluation set.
- Pitfall: Measuring average latency only. Focus on p95/p99 for UX-sensitive features.

Optional session variants (timeboxed alternatives)
- 90-minute executive summary: remove breakouts, keep demo and decision canvas, deliver a 1-page recommendation.
- Half-day deep-dive: add a hands-on lab where we deploy a small dedicated pool and run load tests.

Follow-up cadence and owners (example)
- Within 48 hours: SEs deliver Decision Matrix PDF and experiment runbooks (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Week 1: Customer runs Experiment #1, shares logs (owner: Customer infra lead).
- Week 2: Checkpoint call to review experiment outcomes and decide canary rollout window (owner: Solutions SE).

Parking lot (questions to defer)
- Longer-term model training/finetuning implications.
- Billing contract specifics and reserved capacity pricing (escalate to sales).

Quick run-of-show script for the facilitator (bullet prompts)
- 00:00 — "Welcome, quick intro. We'll deliver 3 concrete experiments and a recommended config by EOD."
- 00:10 — "Customer, 10-minute status — please focus on the traffic shape and SLOs."
- 00:35 — "We'll step through patterns that map to your constraints."
- 01:05 — "Breakout instructions: create 3-line estimate and one key assumption each."
- 01:40 — "Let's pick the top experiment with clear metrics and assign an owner."
- End — "Confirm owners, next meeting, and I'll send artifacts within 48 hours."

Notes about data privacy and security during the session
- Avoid pasting production PII into shared Miro/Google Docs. If necessary, mask or provide a redacted sample.
- If the customer insists on on-prem details, switch to private-deployments follow-up and record action item for an NDA if needed.

Estimated staffing & roles (recommended)
- Lead facilitator (Solutions SE) — runs the room and keeps time.
- Technical co-facilitator (Infra SE) — answers infra-specific questions and helps design experiments.
- Product/PM (customer) — clarifies business tolerance.
- Cloud/infra lead (customer) — confirms access for experiments.

Appendix: sample Experiment Runbook (text)
- Name: "Enable prefix caching + measure p95"
- Owner: <name>
- Hypothesis: "Prefix caching will reduce p95 latency by >=20% for repeated prompts without increasing cost >5%"
- Metric: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate
- Baseline: collect 24h baseline before change
- Success threshold: p95 reduction >=20% AND cost change <=5%
- Duration: 72h A/B test
- Rollback criteria: error rate >0.5% OR p95 regression vs baseline OR quality degradation reported by DS

End of doc.
